records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: A patient undergoes maxillofacial surgery, during which the surgeon accidentally injures the facial nerve. Which of the following muscles is affected:
records.explanation: The buccinator muscle is innervated by the facial nerve. The masseter, mylohyoid and tensor tympani muscles are innervated by the mandibular nerve. The stylopharyngeus is innervated by the glossopharyngeal nerve. Vv

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: The oculomotor nerve supplies all of the following muscles EXCEPT for the: (x) Medial rectus 2%
records.explanation: The oculomotor nerve supplies four extraocular muscles - the inferior oblique, superior rectus, inferior rectus and medial rectus muscles. The superior oblique muscle is innervated by the trochlear nerve, and the lateral rectus muscle by the abducens nerve. Vv

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: Ww The vagus nerve exits the skull through the:
records.explanation: The vagus nerve exits the skull through the jugular foramen. Vv

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: Regarding the olfactory nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT: (x) The olfactory bulb lies in the posterior cranial fossa. 10% The olfactory nerve is the longest cranial nerve. 7%
options: The olfactory nerve originates from the medulla oblongata.
The olfactory nerve carries crude touch sensation from the nasal cavity.
The olfactory tract runs inferiorly to the frontal lobe.
records.explanation: The olfactory nerve is the shortest cranial nerve and originates from the cerebrum; it is one of two nerves that do not originate from the brainstem, the other being the optic nerve. Olfactory nerve fibres enter the skull via the cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone to enter to olfactory bulb in the anterior cranial fossa before passing into the olfactory tract which lies inferior to the frontal lobe. } Vv

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: Regarding the vagus nerve, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: The vagus nerve is a motor and sensory nerve. a The vagus nerve originates in the medulla. 4%
The vagus nerve exits the skull via the jugular foramen.
It is the afferent nerve of the gag reflex.
It innervates the palatoglossal muscle of the tongue.
records.explanation: The vagus nerve is the efferent nerve of the gag reflex (the glossopharyngeal nerve is the afferent nerve). Vv

records.subject: Anatomy
records.stem: Which of the following nerves is the afferent pathway of the corneal blink reflex:
records.explanation: The ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve is the afferent pathway of the corneal blink reflex. The facial nerve is the efferent pathway of the corneal blink reflex. Vv

records.stem: A 64 year old man presents to ED with progressive hearing loss in his left ear, together with drooping of his left lip and complaints of food collecting in his left oral vestibule. Imaging shows a tumour compressing which of the following structures:
records.explanation: The vestibular nerve and facial nerve pass through the internal acoustic meatus, which would account for loss of hearing and weakness of facial muscles respectively. Geo Vv
